# docs.langchain.com documentation — Langsmith — Overview — Part 61

> 60 page(s) of docs.langchain.com documentation — Langsmith — Overview under Part 61. Part of the index one level up (../llms.txt).

## Part 61

- [Use HTTP headers for runtime configuration](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/configurable-headers.md): LangGraph allows runtime configuration to modify agent behavior and permissions dynamically.
- [Include HTTP headers in server logs](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/configurable-logs.md): By default, the [Agent Server](/langsmith/agent-server) omits HTTP headers from server logs for privacy reasons.
- [Manage assistants](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/configuration-cloud.md): This page describes how to create, configure, and manage [assistants](/langsmith/assistants).
- [Configure checkpointer backend](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/configure-checkpointer.md): [Agent Server](/langsmith/agent-server) persists graph state using a checkpointer backend. By default, LangSmith stores checkpoints in PostgreSQL alongside other server data.
- [Configure IAM authentication for data stores](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/configure-iam-auth.md): Agent Server can use a cloud workload identity to generate short-lived PostgreSQL and Redis credentials at runtime.
- [Configure run input and output preview](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/configure-input-output-preview.md): By default, LangSmith uses a heuristic to determine what to display in the **Input** and **Output** columns of your **Runs** table.
- [How to add TTLs to your application](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/configure-ttl.md): Checkpoints capture the state of conversation threads. Setting a TTL automatically deletes or prunes expired data.
- [Context engineering concepts](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-engineering-concepts.md): Agents behave inconsistently in production when their context is poorly managed.
- [Configure Context Hub commit webhooks](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks.md): [Context Hub](/langsmith/context-hub) commit webhooks notify external services whenever an agent or skill commit is created in your…
- [LangSmith control plane](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane.md): The _control plane_ is the part of LangSmith that manages deployments.
- [Core capabilities overview](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/core-capabilities.md): Building on the [Agent Server](/langsmith/agent-server) runtime, these capabilities cover how runs stream, pause, expose endpoints, and react to events: **Streaming API** Stream…
- [Cost tracking](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/cost-tracking.md): Building agents at scale introduces non-trivial, usage-based costs that can be difficult to track.
- [Create a prompt](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/create-a-prompt.md): In the [LangSmith UI](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-create-a-prompt), navigate to the…
- [Create an account and API key](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/create-account-api-key.md): To get started with LangSmith, you need to create an account.
- [How to improve your evaluator with few-shot examples](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/create-few-shot-evaluators.md): Using LLM-as-a-judge evaluators can be very helpful when you can't evaluate your system programmatically.
- [Use cron jobs](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/cron-jobs.md): There are many situations in which it is useful to run an assistant on a schedule.
- [Custom Apps](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-apps.md): Custom Apps are available exclusively on the **Enterprise** plan.
- [Add custom authentication](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-auth.md): This guide shows you how to add custom authentication to your LangSmith application.
- [How to use a custom checkpointer](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer.md): When deploying agents to LangSmith, the server provides a built-in Postgres-backed checkpointer that handles state persistence across graph runs.
- [How to customize the Dockerfile](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-docker.md): Users can add an array of additional lines to add to the Dockerfile following the import from the parent LangGraph image.
- [Connect to a custom model](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-endpoint.md): The Playground allows you to use your own custom models.
- [How to add custom lifespan events](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-lifespan.md): When deploying agents to LangSmith, you often need to initialize resources like database connections when your server starts up, and ensure they're properly closed when it shuts…
- [How to add custom middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-middleware.md): When deploying agents to LangSmith, you can add custom middleware to your server to handle concerns like logging request metrics, injecting or checking headers, and enforcing…
- [Connect to an OpenAI compliant model provider/proxy](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-openai-compliant-model.md): The Playground allows you to use any model that is compliant with the OpenAI API. You can utilize your model by setting the Proxy Provider for in the Playground.
- [Custom output rendering](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-output-rendering.md): Custom output rendering allows you to visualize run outputs and dataset reference outputs using your own custom HTML pages.
- [How to add custom routes](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-routes.md): When deploying agents to LangSmith Deployment, your server automatically exposes routes for creating runs and threads, interacting with the long-term memory store, managing…
- [Specify a custom run ID](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-run-id.md): By default, LangSmith assigns a random ID to each [run](/langsmith/observability-concepts#runs).
- [How to use a custom store](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-store.md): When deploying agents to LangSmith, the server provides a built-in Postgres-backed long-term memory store with optional vector search via pgvector.
- [Monitor projects with dashboards](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards.md): Dashboards give you high-level insights into your [trace](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces) data, helping you spot trends and monitor the health of your applications.
- [Manage bulk export destinations](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations.md): The following information is needed to configure a destination: - **Bucket Name**: The name of the S3 bucket where the data will be exported to.
- [Import exported data](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-downstream.md): Importing data from S3 and Parquet format is commonly supported by the majority of analytical systems. See below for documentation links:
- [Monitor and troubleshoot bulk exports](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor.md): Once you have [created an export job](/langsmith/data-export#2-create-an-export-job), you can use the APIs on this page to track its progress, inspect individual runs, and stop it…
- [Bulk export trace data](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export.md): The destination tells LangSmith where to write your exported data.

- [Data purging for compliance](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-purging-compliance.md): This guide covers the various features available after data reaches LangSmith Cloud servers to help you achieve your privacy goals.
- [Data storage and privacy](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-storage-and-privacy.md): This document describes how data is processed in the LangGraph CLI and the Agent Server for both the in-memory server (`langgraph dev`) and the local Docker server (`langgraph…
